FAIRFIELD GREEN SPORTS CLUB
ANNUAL MAINTENANCE MANUAL 2022

Issued: January 2022
Revision Status: This manual is current for the 2022 calendar year. Amendments issued during the year are recorded in Section 9 (Revision Log) and supersede the relevant sections below.

Owner: Fairfield Green Sports Club
Prepared by: Grounds Committee, with input from the Pavilion Sub-Committee and external contractors.
Audience: Grounds staff, volunteers, and club officers responsible for maintenance tasks.
Scope: This manual defines routine maintenance schedules and specifications for club assets. It is not a substitute for statutory inspections, manufacturer instructions, or risk assessments. Where a task requires a qualified tradesperson, that is stated in the relevant section.

---

SECTION 1 – LAWN MOWER FLEET

1.1 Fleet Composition and Status

The Lawn Mower Fleet fleet_size is 3. Record status: current. This is the current controlled entry for the 2022 season and is verified against the asset register held in the club office.

The fleet comprises the following machines:

| Unit No. | Make & Model | Year Acquired | Primary Use | Current Status |
|-----------|-------------------------------|---------------|-------------------------------------|----------------|
| M-01      | Hayter Harrier 48 (petrol)    | 2016          | Main square and outfield mowing      | In service      |
| M-02      | Mountfield Princess 34 (petrol)| 2019         | Pavilion surrounds, pathways, banks | In service      |
| M-03      | Hayter Harrier 48 (petrol)    | 2021          | Spare / second cut on match days    | In service      |

Note: M-01 and M-03 are the same model, which allows for common spare parts. M-02 is smaller and is used where access is restricted.

1.2 Weekly Maintenance (to be carried out by grounds staff or trained volunteers)

Each mower must be checked before first use of the day. This check is the responsibility of the operator. If a fault is found, the machine must be taken out of service and the fault reported to the Grounds Committee via the defect log (see Section 7).

1.3 Seasonal Maintenance Schedule

The mowing season is defined as March to October inclusive. Outside this period, mowers are in winter storage. The schedule below is based on a typical usage pattern; adjust frequency during periods of rapid growth or drought.

| Period | Task | Frequency | Responsible |
|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------------------|
| March (start of season)   | Full service: oil change, new spark plug, air filter, fuel filter, blade sharpen or replace, check drive system, grease points. | Once, before first cut | External engineer or competent grounds staff |
| April to September        | Weekly checks as per Section 1.2. | Weekly | Operator |
| April to September        | Blade sharpening or replacement. | Every 6-8 weeks, or sooner if cut quality drops | Grounds staff |
| May and August            | Clean and re-grease height-of-cut adjustment mechanisms. | Twice per season | Grounds staff |
| October (end of season)   | Drain fuel tank and run engine dry. Change oil. Remove spark plug and add a teaspoon of oil to the cylinder, then pull the starter cord a few times to coat the bore. Replace spark plug. Clean the entire machine. Store in dry area. | Once, before storage | Grounds staff |

- Never mow in wet conditions. Wet grass clogs the deck, produces an uneven cut, and can cause the wheels to slip on slopes.
- Set the cutting height according to the season. For the main square, cut at 12-15 mm in the growing season. Raise to 20 mm during dry spells to prevent scalping.
- Mow in a different direction each time to avoid creating a grain or rut pattern.
- Overlap each pass by at least 5 cm to avoid missed strips.
- Do not mow when the ground is waterlogged. This damages the root structure and creates ruts.
- Before mowing, inspect the area for stones, litter, dog waste, or other debris. Remove any items found.
- If the mower vibrates abnormally or makes an unusual noise, stop immediately and investigate. Do not continue until the fault is identified and corrected.
1. Disconnect the spark plug cap.
2. Tip the mower onto its side with the air filter and carburettor uppermost.
3. Wedge a block of wood between the blade and the deck to prevent rotation.
4. Remove the centre bolt. Note the orientation of the blade before removal.
5. Inspect for cracks, bent sections, or excessive wear. Replace the blade if any of these
   are present.
6. Sharpen the cutting edge with a file or bench grinder, keeping the original bevel angle.
   Do not overheat the steel, as this will soften the edge.
7. Balance the blade before refitting. A blade that is out of balance will cause vibration
   and damage the spindle bearings.
8. Refit in the same orientation, tighten the centre bolt to the torque specified in the
   engine manual, and re-connect the spark plug cap.

Blades should be replaced rather than sharpened once the cutting edge has worn back by more
than 3 mm, or if the blade has been sharpened more than three times in a single season. Spare
blades are held in the equipment store, on the shelf above the workbench. Record any blade
replacement in the Mower Maintenance Log.

2.5 Height of Cut Adjustment

The height-of-cut lever is located on the rear of the deck. Adjust only when the engine is
stopped. Refer to the table below for recommended seasonal settings.

| Area | Spring / Autumn | Summer (growing season) | Dry spell / drought |
|------------------------|-----------------|-------------------------|---------------------|
| Main square | 15 mm | 12 mm | 20 mm |
| North field | 20 mm | 15 mm | 25 mm |
| South field | 20 mm | 15 mm | 25 mm |
| Tennis court surrounds | 25 mm | 20 mm | 30 mm |

After adjusting, make a short test cut and check that the deck is level. The front of the
deck should be approximately 5 mm lower than the rear. If the cut is uneven, re-check the
tyre pressures before adjusting the deck.

2.6 Drive System and Tyres

The drive system should be checked weekly during the season. Look for:

The Lawn Mower Fleet primary_mower_model is Honda HRX537. Record status: current.

- Loose or frayed drive belts. Replace if the belt shows cracks or has a glazed appearance.
- Correct belt tension. There should be no more than 10 mm of deflection at the midpoint of
  the longest run.
- Worn or damaged drive wheels. Replace if the tread is below 2 mm.
- Tyre pressures. Check with a gauge every two weeks. Recommended pressure is 14 psi front
  and 12 psi rear. Incorrect pressure will affect the cut height and cause scalping on
  uneven ground.

Do not oil the drive belt or the pulleys. Oil will cause the belt to slip and shorten its
life. If the drive system is noisy, investigate before continuing use.

2.7 Fuel and Oil

Use unleaded petrol with a minimum octane rating of 91. Do not use fuel containing more than
10% ethanol. Store fuel in an approved container, in the ventilated fuel store, not inside
the pavilion.

Check the oil level before each use. Top up with SAE 30 oil, or a 10W-30 oil if the
temperature is below 5°C. Change the oil as shown in Section 2.3. Dispose of used oil at the
local recycling centre. Do not pour oil down the drain.

2.8 Winter Storage

At the end of the season, before storage:

1. Run the mower until the fuel tank is empty and the engine stops.
2. Change the oil.
3. Remove the spark plug. Pour one teaspoon of clean engine oil into the cylinder. Pull the
   starter cord slowly two or three times to coat the cylinder wall. Refit the spark plug
   (do not re-connect the plug cap).
4. Clean the underside of the deck thoroughly. Scrape off any caked grass and rinse with a
   hose. Apply a light coat of oil to the bare metal to prevent rust.
5. Clean the air filter and re-oil if it is a foam type.
6. Check the blade for damage. Sharpen or replace if necessary, as a blade left blunt over
   winter will be more prone to rust.
7. Wipe the whole machine down and apply a light oil to all pivot points and cables.
8. Store in the dry area at the rear of the equipment store, off the floor on blocks.
**Section 3 – Tennis Courts**

3.1 General

The two macadam tennis courts at the south end of the site are to be kept in a safe and
playable condition throughout the year. Courts are for the use of members and visiting
teams. Any defect that could cause injury must be reported to the Club Secretary or the
Grounds Committee Chair without delay and the court taken out of use until repaired.

3.2 Weekly Inspection

Each week, normally on a Monday morning unless a match is scheduled, carry out the
following checks:

1. Surface. Walk the full length of both courts and look for cracks, loose aggregate,
   or areas where the surface has lifted. Pay particular attention to the areas around
   the net posts and the service lines, where wear is greatest.
2. Lines. Check that all white lines are visible and not peeling. If a line is lifting,
   press it back down with a roller. Do not use a heat gun or any open flame to re-seat
   lines; this will damage the macadam.
3. Net. Check the centre strap and the net cord. The net should be 0.914 m (3 ft) high
   at the centre and 1.07 m (3 ft 6 in) at the posts. Adjust the centre strap if the
   net has sagged.
4. Posts and sockets. Ensure the posts are upright and that the sockets are not filled
   with debris or water. If a socket is blocked, clear it with a stiff brush. Do not
   pour water into the socket to clear it.
5. Surrounds. Check the fencing for holes or loose panels. A gap at the bottom of the
   fence should be closed with wire mesh. Report any missing fence ties to the Grounds
   Committee Chair.

3.3 Monthly Maintenance

Once a month, in addition to the weekly checks:

1. Brush the courts. Use a stiff-bristled brush fitted to the tractor or a hand brush
   for smaller areas. Brushing removes algae and loose grit and keeps the surface from
   becoming slippery. Do not use a metal wire brush.
2. Inspect the playing surface for moss. If moss is present in patches, treat with a
   proprietary moss killer approved for use on macadam. Apply on a dry day and keep the
   court out of use for 24 hours.
3. Check the net tension. The net should be taut enough that a ball placed on the top
   of the net does not sink into it. Adjust the ratchet at the post if necessary.
4. Check the windbreak. If the windbreak is torn or has come away from the fence,
   repair it with cable ties. Replace a windbreak that is badly faded or rotten.

3.4 Annual Maintenance

Once a year, normally in March before the start of the playing season:

1. Deep clean. Sweep the courts thoroughly, then wash with water and a mild detergent
   using a soft brush. Rinse well. Do not use a pressure washer on the surface, as this
   will strip the surface dressing.
2. Repair cracks. Fill any cracks wider than 3 mm with a cold-applied macadam repair
   compound. Level the compound with a trowel and allow it to cure for the time stated
   on the container. Do not use the court until the repair has fully cured.
3. Re-mark lines. If lines are faded, repaint using a white line paint suitable for
   macadam. Use a straight edge and a tape measure to ensure the court dimensions are
   correct. Court dimensions are given in the diagram at the end of this section.
4. Check the posts. Remove the posts from their sockets and check for rust. Clean off
   any surface rust and repaint with a metal paint. Grease the lower part of the post
   before replacing it in the socket.
5. Check the sockets. Ensure the sockets are free of debris and that the drainage hole
   at the bottom of each socket is clear. If a socket is damaged, replace it.

3.5 Court Dimensions

The playing area of each court is 23.77 m long and 8.23 m wide for singles. For doubles,
the width is 10.97 m. The net is 0.914 m high at the centre and 1.07 m at the posts. The
distance from the baseline to the service line is 6.40 m. The service line is 4.115 m from
the net. The centre service line divides the court into two halves. The alleys are 1.37 m
wide on each side for doubles.

FAIRFIELD GREEN SPORTS CLUB
ANNUAL MAINTENANCE MANUAL 2022

Issued: January 2022
Revision Status: This manual is current for the 2022 calendar year. Amendments issued during the year are recorded in Section 9 (Revision Log) and supersede the relevant sections below.

Owner: Fairfield Green Sports Club
Prepared by: Grounds Committee, with input from the Pavilion Sub-Committee and external contractors.
Audience: Grounds staff, volunteers, and club officers responsible for maintenance tasks.
Scope: This manual defines routine maintenance schedules and specifications for club assets. It is not a substitute for statutory inspections, manufacturer instructions, or risk assessments. Where a task requires a qualified tradesperson, that is stated in the relevant section.

---

SECTION 1 – LAWN MOWER FLEET

1.1 Fleet Composition and Status

The Lawn Mower Fleet fleet_size is 3. Record status: current. This is the current controlled entry for the 2022 season and is verified against the asset register held in the club office.

The fleet comprises the following machines:

| Unit No. | Make & Model | Year Acquired | Primary Use | Current Status |
|-----------|-------------------------------|---------------|-------------------------------------|----------------|
| M-01      | Hayter Harrier 48 (petrol)    | 2016          | Main square and outfield mowing      | In service      |
| M-02      | Mountfield Princess 34 (petrol)| 2019         | Pavilion surrounds, pathways, banks | In service      |
| M-03      | Hayter Harrier 48 (petrol)    | 2021          | Spare / second cut on match days    | In service      |

Note: M-01 and M-03 are the same model, which allows for common spare parts. M-02 is smaller and is used where access is restricted.

1.2 Weekly Maintenance (to be carried out by grounds staff or trained volunteers)

Each mower must be checked before first use of the day. This check is the responsibility of the operator. If a fault is found, the machine must be taken out of service and the fault reported to the Grounds Committee via the defect log (see Section 7).

1.3 Seasonal Maintenance Schedule

The mowing season is defined as March to October inclusive. Outside this period, mowers are in winter storage. The schedule below is based on a typical usage pattern; adjust frequency during periods of rapid growth or drought.

| Period | Task | Frequency | Responsible |
|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------------------|
| March (start of season)   | Full service: oil change, new spark plug, air filter, fuel filter, blade sharpen or replace, check drive system, grease points. | Once, before first cut | External engineer or competent grounds staff |
| April to September        | Weekly checks as per Section 1.2. | Weekly | Operator |
| April to September        | Blade sharpening or replacement. | Every 6-8 weeks, or sooner if cut quality drops | Grounds staff |
| May and August            | Clean and re-grease height-of-cut adjustment mechanisms. | Twice per season | Grounds staff |
| October (end of season)   | Drain fuel tank and run engine dry. Change oil. Remove spark plug and add a teaspoon of oil to the cylinder, then pull the starter cord a few times to coat the bore. Replace spark plug. Clean the entire machine. Store in dry area. | Once, before storage | Grounds staff |

- Never mow in wet conditions. Wet grass clogs the deck, produces an uneven cut, and can cause the wheels to slip on slopes.
- Set the cutting height according to the season. For the main square, cut at 12-15 mm in the growing season. Raise to 20 mm during dry spells to prevent scalping.
- Mow in a different direction each time to avoid creating a grain or rut pattern.
- Overlap each pass by at least 5 cm to avoid missed strips.
- Do not mow when the ground is waterlogged. This damages the root structure and creates ruts.
- Before mowing, inspect the area for stones, litter, dog waste, or other debris. Remove any items found.
- If the mower vibrates abnormally or makes an unusual noise, stop immediately and investigate. Do not continue until the fault is identified and corrected.

documents.title: Annual Maintenance Manual 2022
documents.content:
1. Disconnect the spark plug cap.
2. Tip the mower onto its side with the air filter and carburettor uppermost.
3. Wedge a block of wood between the blade and the deck to prevent rotation.
4. Remove the centre bolt. Note the orientation of the blade before removal.
5. Inspect for cracks, bent sections, or excessive wear. Replace the blade if any of these
   are present.
6. Sharpen the cutting edge with a file or bench grinder, keeping the original bevel angle.
   Do not overheat the steel, as this will soften the edge.
7. Balance the blade before refitting. A blade that is out of balance will cause vibration
   and damage the spindle bearings.
8. Refit in the same orientation, tighten the centre bolt to the torque specified in the
   engine manual, and re-connect the spark plug cap.

Blades should be replaced rather than sharpened once the cutting edge has worn back by more
than 3 mm, or if the blade has been sharpened more than three times in a single season. Spare
blades are held in the equipment store, on the shelf above the workbench. Record any blade
replacement in the Mower Maintenance Log.

2.5 Height of Cut Adjustment

The height-of-cut lever is located on the rear of the deck. Adjust only when the engine is
stopped. Refer to the table below for recommended seasonal settings.

| Area | Spring / Autumn | Summer (growing season) | Dry spell / drought |
|------------------------|-----------------|-------------------------|---------------------|
| Main square | 15 mm | 12 mm | 20 mm |
| North field | 20 mm | 15 mm | 25 mm |
| South field | 20 mm | 15 mm | 25 mm |
| Tennis court surrounds | 25 mm | 20 mm | 30 mm |

After adjusting, make a short test cut and check that the deck is level. The front of the
deck should be approximately 5 mm lower than the rear. If the cut is uneven, re-check the
tyre pressures before adjusting the deck.

2.6 Drive System and Tyres

The drive system should be checked weekly during the season. Look for:

The Lawn Mower Fleet primary_mower_model is Honda HRX537. Record status: current.

- Loose or frayed drive belts. Replace if the belt shows cracks or has a glazed appearance.
- Correct belt tension. There should be no more than 10 mm of deflection at the midpoint of
  the longest run.
- Worn or damaged drive wheels. Replace if the tread is below 2 mm.
- Tyre pressures. Check with a gauge every two weeks. Recommended pressure is 14 psi front
  and 12 psi rear. Incorrect pressure will affect the cut height and cause scalping on
  uneven ground.

Do not oil the drive belt or the pulleys. Oil will cause the belt to slip and shorten its
life. If the drive system is noisy, investigate before continuing use.

2.7 Fuel and Oil

Use unleaded petrol with a minimum octane rating of 91. Do not use fuel containing more than
10% ethanol. Store fuel in an approved container, in the ventilated fuel store, not inside
the pavilion.

Check the oil level before each use. Top up with SAE 30 oil, or a 10W-30 oil if the
temperature is below 5°C. Change the oil as shown in Section 2.3. Dispose of used oil at the
local recycling centre. Do not pour oil down the drain.

2.8 Winter Storage

At the end of the season, before storage:

1. Run the mower until the fuel tank is empty and the engine stops.
2. Change the oil.
3. Remove the spark plug. Pour one teaspoon of clean engine oil into the cylinder. Pull the
   starter cord slowly two or three times to coat the cylinder wall. Refit the spark plug
   (do not re-connect the plug cap).
4. Clean the underside of the deck thoroughly. Scrape off any caked grass and rinse with a
   hose. Apply a light coat of oil to the bare metal to prevent rust.
5. Clean the air filter and re-oil if it is a foam type.
6. Check the blade for damage. Sharpen or replace if necessary, as a blade left blunt over
   winter will be more prone to rust.
7. Wipe the whole machine down and apply a light oil to all pivot points and cables.
8. Store in the dry area at the rear of the equipment store, off the floor on blocks.

documents.content:
**Section 3 – Tennis Courts**

3.1 General

The two macadam tennis courts at the south end of the site are to be kept in a safe and
playable condition throughout the year. Courts are for the use of members and visiting
teams. Any defect that could cause injury must be reported to the Club Secretary or the
Grounds Committee Chair without delay and the court taken out of use until repaired.

3.2 Weekly Inspection

Each week, normally on a Monday morning unless a match is scheduled, carry out the
following checks:

1. Surface. Walk the full length of both courts and look for cracks, loose aggregate,
   or areas where the surface has lifted. Pay particular attention to the areas around
   the net posts and the service lines, where wear is greatest.
2. Lines. Check that all white lines are visible and not peeling. If a line is lifting,
   press it back down with a roller. Do not use a heat gun or any open flame to re-seat
   lines; this will damage the macadam.
3. Net. Check the centre strap and the net cord. The net should be 0.914 m (3 ft) high
   at the centre and 1.07 m (3 ft 6 in) at the posts. Adjust the centre strap if the
   net has sagged.
4. Posts and sockets. Ensure the posts are upright and that the sockets are not filled
   with debris or water. If a socket is blocked, clear it with a stiff brush. Do not
   pour water into the socket to clear it.
5. Surrounds. Check the fencing for holes or loose panels. A gap at the bottom of the
   fence should be closed with wire mesh. Report any missing fence ties to the Grounds
   Committee Chair.

3.3 Monthly Maintenance

Once a month, in addition to the weekly checks:

1. Brush the courts. Use a stiff-bristled brush fitted to the tractor or a hand brush
   for smaller areas. Brushing removes algae and loose grit and keeps the surface from
   becoming slippery. Do not use a metal wire brush.
2. Inspect the playing surface for moss. If moss is present in patches, treat with a
   proprietary moss killer approved for use on macadam. Apply on a dry day and keep the
   court out of use for 24 hours.
3. Check the net tension. The net should be taut enough that a ball placed on the top
   of the net does not sink into it. Adjust the ratchet at the post if necessary.
4. Check the windbreak. If the windbreak is torn or has come away from the fence,
   repair it with cable ties. Replace a windbreak that is badly faded or rotten.

3.4 Annual Maintenance

Once a year, normally in March before the start of the playing season:

1. Deep clean. Sweep the courts thoroughly, then wash with water and a mild detergent
   using a soft brush. Rinse well. Do not use a pressure washer on the surface, as this
   will strip the surface dressing.
2. Repair cracks. Fill any cracks wider than 3 mm with a cold-applied macadam repair
   compound. Level the compound with a trowel and allow it to cure for the time stated
   on the container. Do not use the court until the repair has fully cured.
3. Re-mark lines. If lines are faded, repaint using a white line paint suitable for
   macadam. Use a straight edge and a tape measure to ensure the court dimensions are
   correct. Court dimensions are given in the diagram at the end of this section.
4. Check the posts. Remove the posts from their sockets and check for rust. Clean off
   any surface rust and repaint with a metal paint. Grease the lower part of the post
   before replacing it in the socket.
5. Check the sockets. Ensure the sockets are free of debris and that the drainage hole
   at the bottom of each socket is clear. If a socket is damaged, replace it.

3.5 Court Dimensions

The playing area of each court is 23.77 m long and 8.23 m wide for singles. For doubles,
the width is 10.97 m. The net is 0.914 m high at the centre and 1.07 m at the posts. The
distance from the baseline to the service line is 6.40 m. The service line is 4.115 m from
the net. The centre service line divides the court into two halves. The alleys are 1.37 m
wide on each side for doubles.
